title: 10n + 5 throws TypeError instead of just giving you 15
assumption: Any two things that look like numbers can be added together directly.

input.description: Mixing a value that came from a BigInt-returning source (e.g. a large parsed id, `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` workaround, or a library that returns BigInt) with an ordinary numeric literal elsewhere in arithmetic.

what_goes_wrong: Introducing a single `BigInt` value into a codebase that otherwise uses plain `number` breaks at the first arithmetic operation that mixes the two, with a runtime `TypeError` rather than a silent or compile-time-caught issue.
why: `BigInt` and `Number` are deliberately kept as separate, non-interoperable types in JavaScript: implicitly coercing one to the other would either lose a BigInt's exactness (converting to Number) or silently change comparison/arithmetic semantics, so the spec requires an explicit conversion (`BigInt(5)` or `Number(10n)`) before the two can be combined with `+`, `-`, `*`, etc. (Comparison operators like `<` and `==` are a deliberate exception and do work across the two types.)

repros.expected_output:
TypeError: Cannot mix BigInt and other types, use explicit conversions
15n
true

repros.code:
# Python has only one built-in integer type, so there is nothing to mix:
# int already has unlimited precision, no separate 'big integer' type exists.
print(10 + 5, type(10 + 5))

fix: Convert explicitly at the boundary where a value becomes a BigInt (or stays a Number) and keep the two types from mixing in arithmetic; don't let a single BigInt-returning call silently propagate into number-typed code.
